root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `1 << bcf_type_shift[t] <= end - p` before `*val = le_to_i32(p)` may execute.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When the first FORMAT byte selects `BCF_BT_INT32`, the decoder must require the full 4-byte payload width implied by `t` to fit within the remaining bytes before entering the INT32 decode path.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable guard compares `end - p` against the shift exponent `bcf_type_shift[t]` (2 for `BCF_BT_INT32`) instead of the byte width `1 << bcf_type_shift[t]` (4), so the 2-byte remainder is admitted and the 32-bit read proceeds.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable guard, the check-width operand remains the shift exponent `bcf_type_shift[t] = 2`, which equals the two remaining payload bytes and therefore does not reject the truncated INT32 field.

Immediately before `*val = le_to_i32(p)`, the INT32 read end `p + (1 << bcf_type_shift[t])` is already past `end`, so the decode call forwards an out-of-bounds 4-byte read into the inlined `le_to_u32()` sink.

edges.relation: The same type-derived width that the root guard should have enforced is the 4-byte read width consumed by the subsequent INT32 decode call.
The truncated typed-value pointer that the root guard leaves unbounded is the same pointer later passed as `p` into the INT32 decode call.
